labctl.notes: exec: labctl exec alto "<cmd>" (ssh root@:5843, key bridge_key) reaches the Debian KIOSK, not the Alto -- the emulated machine has no shell and no network. Drive the Alto itself with labctl type/key (it is paced at 66/66 ms, two Alto fields) or with the tile's own alto-drive.py, which leads modifiers by a gap and can measure ink in a rect.

reset.fixture: The Alto Executive on the Non-Programmer's Disk, untouched, on a 608x808 root -- the machine's honest empty state rather than an application. That is deliberate and it follows plus4: an earlier plan baked the golden INSIDE Bravo so a visitor would land in the first WYSIWYG word processor with no 30-second wait, and 10ae428 had already rejected exactly that on the Plus/4 because arriving mid-application tells a visitor nothing about what they are looking at. The choice of application lives in the exhibit UI instead: the alto keyboard profile's first row is ?, BRAVO and DRAW, one Executive command each -- Laurel is deliberately absent, because the mail reader wants a Grapevine server this tile has no Ethernet for and answers with a blank page and an hourglass. Certified 2026-08-10 by framebuffer, after the bake so nothing it did could reach the golden: typing ? filled an empty screen body with the disk's directory, Bravo 7.5 took the screen from the Executive, a 35-character line typed into it intact at 66/66 ms, and the three mouse buttons produced Bravo's own three selections -- RED/left one character, YELLOW/middle the whole word, BLUE/right the selection extended. loadvm golden then returned the untouched Executive with the visitor's session gone.

museum.arch: Xerox Alto II XM: a custom TTL processor
eraSoftware: the Alto Executive, the command prompt this exhibit rests at
museum.periodBrowser: none -- PARC had Ethernet, laser printing and electronic mail two decades before the web had a first page
museum.blurb: The machine that invented the screen you are reading this on: overlapping windows, a mouse with buttons, a what-you-see-is-what-you-get editor and Ethernet, all in 1973, none of them for sale. Its display stands on end because it is a sheet of paper -- 606 by 808 dots, 8.5 by 11 inches -- and that is why every document window since has been taller than it is wide.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 12 kiosk runs ContrAlto 2 (jdersch/Contralto2, BSD-3-Clause, .NET 8 + Avalonia, pinned at e3681fbc) as an Alto II XM. Zero external media -- the Alto I and Alto II microcode PROMs and eight Diablo disk packs ship inside the emulator's own repository and arrive with the source it is built from, so nothing is downloaded, staged or committed; the exhibit boots nonprog.dsk, the Non-Programmer's Disk, whose sha256 the builder asserts. THE ONLY PORTRAIT EXHIBIT IN THE COLLECTION: the kiosk X root is 608x808, the Alto's own bitmap, so the capture is exactly the machine's picture with no letterbox -- and crt-f.glb, the tall tube it is displayed on in the 3D museum, was modelled for this tile and is used by nothing else. Two upstream patches are required and both are in scripts/build-guests/patches/contralto2-wmless-kiosk.patch: ContrAlto's KioskMode (the only switch that hides its menu and status bars) crashes before the first frame, and with no window manager nothing places the window or gives its display control keyboard focus -- unfixed, every keystroke is dropped silently and the exhibit reads as a dead emulator. MAME's alto2 driver was tried first and never boots here (five packs, 120 s runs, a uniform white field, PC pinned at 1); that negative result is recorded in docs/lab/research/xerox-add.md so nobody pays for it twice. See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/alto.md.
